intro: Translate Excel translates a Excel workbook (XLSX) into another language and gives you back the same file, with the same layout, ready to use. It is useful for catalogues, price lists, inventories, surveys and budgets: you do not have to copy the text into a translator and format the result again.

It translates the text of every cell on every sheet, including text with bold or coloured parts. Numbers, dates, formulas, sheet names (formulas use them), charts, pivot tables and conditional formatting are not touched. Each piece of text keeps its formatting: if a word was bold, italic or in another colour, its translation is too, even if it moves within the sentence.

Choose the target language among Spanish, English, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Catalan, Dutch, Polish, Romanian, Galician and Basque; the original language is detected automatically or you can set it. In “Terms not to translate” you can list brand, product or people's names, one per line, so they stay as they are in the translated workbook.

The translation is done by a free AI model through OpenRouter, with your consent and within your plan's AI requests; repeated text is translated once and text with no letters (figures, codes) is not sent. Machine translation can contain errors, so review the workbook before sending or publishing it.
steps: Choose the target language and, optionally, the terms not to translate.

faq.a: Not in the usual cases: only the text changes. Numbers, dates, formulas, sheet names (formulas use them), charts, pivot tables and conditional formatting are not touched.

faq.q: How much text can be translated?
faq.a: Up to about 400,000 characters per workbook, roughly 150 pages. If it is longer, split it first.
The text is sent to the AI model only to translate it, with your consent; the file is deleted when it expires.
